task.description: WF-02 Step 2a (ELIXIR-DEV) for run-id WF02-REQ021-20260816: implement lib/letflow/design/req021-auth-plug-pipeline.md (CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR PASS) exactly -- Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline and Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus, the Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier behaviour seam plus its real oidcc-backed and test-double implementations, wiring together Letflow.Identity's four existing functions, Letflow.Oidc.ClaimMapping.map_verified_claims/3, and the tenant write-pause check. router.ex left unmodified per the design's own §8 decision.
acceptance_criteria: a request with a valid OIDC bearer token (or a test double standing in for ueberauth_oidcc's verification result, if a real Keycloak issuer isn't reachable in this environment -- state explicitly which was used) flows through verify -> tenant resolution -> realm-ownership guard -> JIT provisioning and ends with an auth context (user_id, tenant_id, roles) available to the next plug in the chain
a request with a missing or malformed bearer token is rejected with 401 before tenant resolution or JIT provisioning runs
a write request (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE) against a tenant whose status is migrating is rejected with 503 and a Retry-After header; a GET/HEAD request against the same tenant passes through
a request whose token's realm does not match the resolved tenant's bound realm is rejected, not silently JIT-provisioned under the wrong tenant
moduledoc explicitly states this plug supersedes REQ-103 (never built) as Letflow's first real auth plug, and names which router.ex routes (if any) it is mounted in front of

result.summary: Implemented lib/letflow/design/req021-auth-plug-pipeline.md exactly as specified, no deviations from the design's own decisions. New files: lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex (Letflow.Plugs.AuthPipeline, steps 1-4+6 of the design: bearer-token extraction/verification -> tenant resolution from the iss claim's realm suffix -> realm-ownership guard called strictly before JIT provisioning -> JIT provisioning/lookup -> conn.assigns[:auth_context] attachment as one nested map with user_id/tenant_id/roles keys, per design §5.1), lib/letflow/plugs/tenant_status.ex (Letflow.Plugs.TenantStatus, step 5: write-method allowlist short-circuit, tenant status lookup via Repo.get(Tenant, tenant_id), 503+Retry-After:30 on :migrating, fail-closed on a genuine DB error per the design's own §6.4 recommendation -- flagged, not silently chosen, since OQ-14 leaves this to ELIXIR-DEV/REVIEWER judgment), lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier.ex (the Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier behaviour, one callback verify_bearer_token/2, per design §3.2), lib/letflow/oidc/token_verifier/oidcc.ex (the real adapter, Oidcc.ClientContext.from_configuration_worker/3 with client_secret: :unauthenticated + Oidcc.Token.validate_jwt/3, per design §3.1), test/support/token_verifier_double.ex (test-only double under test/support/, matching the design's explicit placement instruction and this project's elixirc_paths(:test) convention -- confirmed compiled only under MIX_ENV=test). Config changes: config/dev.exs and config/test.exs both gained client_id (OQ-2, placeholder value 'letflow-placeholder-client', not secret -- client_secret: :unauthenticated mode performs no real IdP credential auth), signing_algs (OQ-3, resolved to ["RS256"] matching Keycloak's default), and token_verifier (dev: Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifier.Oidcc: test: Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifierDouble) under the existing :oidc key. config/prod.exs left untouched (currently has no :oidc key at all -- 'not yet filled in' per its own comment; adding one now would be speculative config no requirement calls for). router.ex is byte-for-byte unmodified -- confirmed via `git diff --stat lib/letflow/router.ex` returning empty -- per the design's explicit §8 decision (built and tested, zero of the 3 existing non-tenant-scoped routes mounted behind either plug, left for S4). AC1: demonstrated via Letflow.Oidc.TokenVerifierDouble (step 9's explicit instruction) -- NOT the reachable r-co-keycloak-1 container, because (confirmed by design §3.2, independently re-confirmed this session) that container is R-Co's own instance with no confirmed Letflow realm/client, and Letflow's own :oidc config deliberately points at a .invalid placeholder issuer. AC5's moduledoc requirement satisfied in both new plug modules (see lib/letflow/plugs/auth_pipeline.ex and tenant_status.ex module docs -- each states REQ-103 supersession, cites the ported R-Co source file, and states explicitly that zero router.ex routes are mounted behind it today). One implementation decision beyond the design's literal text, made and documented inline (not silently): AuthPipeline.call/2's `with`/`else` chain tags every step's failure reason with which step produced it (e.g. {:error, {:ownership, reason}} vs {:error, {:tenant, reason}}) rather than pattern-matching the bare reason atom directly in the else clause -- necessary because verify_bearer_token/2, resolve_tenant_by_realm/1, and provision_oidc_user/3 all independently use :not_found and other overlapping atoms for unrelated failures, so an untagged else clause could not distinguish e.g. a tenant-resolution 401 from a provisioning 500 sharing the same raw reason. This is a mechanical implementation detail achieving exactly the status-code mapping design §5 specifies, not a behavioral deviation.

issues.description: Design §6.4 (OQ-14) leaves fail-open vs. fail-closed on a genuine DB error during TenantStatus's tenant-status lookup as a recommendation, not a mandate. This implementation follows the design's own stated recommendation (fail-closed: a Repo.get/2 failure is not caught, so it propagates as a crash of the handling process rather than silently passing the write through) -- flagging for REVIEWER to confirm this is the right call, per the design's own request.
